newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakai denies knowledge of illegal subcontracting.
newsitem.headline: Sakai denies knowledge of illegal subcontracting.

text.p: Sakai Moving Service Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it had used a subcontractor for transporting pianos without knowing that the subcontractor was operating without government authorisation.
Transport firms in Japan must obtain the government's approval in order to operate.
Earlier in the day, police raided Sakai Moving in search of evidence of illegal subcontracting. The firm operates cargo and car transport businesses.
The firm said it had confused the Osaka-based subcontractor with another firm of the same name which operates in Tokyo and has a government licence.
The incident would not have a significant impact on its business, Sakai said in a statement.
Osaka-based Sakai Moving's shares were listed on the Osaka Securities Exchange on October 30.
The company's shares dropped 30 yen on Tuesday to close at 4,510 yen.
